newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 4.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Wednesday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* The market is likely to continue to slip on Wednesday in a correction to its recent bull-run.
* BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap said he expects the correction to last up to the end of the week and advises selective buying with the market's downturn.
* Angping & Associates analyst Ju-Ann Reinoso recommends profit-taking on stocks which gained more than 20 percent and a buy-back once the market establishes a support base.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index snapped out of an eight-day rise by closing 17.94 points lower at 2,802.78.
* The Dow Jones on Tuesday ended 22.75 points higher to 7,312.15. PLDT's ADR slipped $0 1/2 to $58 5/8.
* The Philippine peso closed higher at 26.365 to the dollar vs 26.374.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average rose at 16.0625 percent vs 16.03125.

* Philippine Airlines posted a net loss of 1.41 billion pesos in the fourth quarter of the year, ending March 31, compared to a 1.2 billion loss in the third quarter, PAL's unaudited financial statement showed.
* Metro Pacific Corp said its board had approved a 30 percent stock dividend.
* Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes said the bank was studying the possibility of limiting local banks' exposure to consumer loans.
* Globe Telecom said it had awarded $60 million of supply contracts to Fujitsu Ltd and Tomen Corp .
* Pure Foods Corp, food subsidiary of conglomerate Ayala Corp, is negotiating for the local franchise of leading fastfood chain Burger King, company officials said.
* Politics will be pivotal in sustaining Philippine economic growth beyond 1997, regional think-tank Pacific Economic Cooperation Council (PECC) said.
* A journalist who specialised in exposing drug syndicates and police corruption was shot dead in a taxi on Tuesday as he struggled with his assassin, police said.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld said President Clinton restored the duty-free eligibility of Philippine made radio pagers and scanners which were disqualified for benefits under the U.S. Generalised System of Preferences.
* BusinessWorld said the Central Bank may soon remove the $50,000 ceiling on over-the-counter dollar sales to further deregulate the foreign exchange market.

* Manila Bulletin said the House Committee on Energy will open a series of public hearings today on the exclusive 25-year crude supply pact between Petron Corp and its partner Saudi Arabia's Aramco, to determine if the deal continues to benefit the local refiner.
